source: Fitzpatrick, Euclid Elements I.44, PDF pp.42–43 (zero-based), lines1661 onward
problem: Construct an actual proper parallelogram on a prescribed nonzero base, equal in area to a given proper triangle, with a prescribed nonstraight angle.
proof_idea: I23 copies the angle onto the base. I42 fixes its first edge and scales only the second ray to obtain the target area. Transitivity of normalized cosine equality transports the prescribed angle.

comments.route_difference: Analytic positive scaling replaces Euclid complement construction; preserves actual base and angle.
comments.carriers: cart(R,R) points; R+ area; proper triangles and distinct base endpoints
